feature1.prompt: Python Enum values (used to show default values in function signatures) are rendered ugly. Currently, when an enum value is used as a default parameter, it is displayed using its full internal representation (for example, <MyEnum.ValueA: 10>) which makes the signature hard to read. This feature requires modifying the core functionality to produce a cleaner output that simply shows the enum type and its member name (for example, MyEnum.ValueA). The expected behavior is that function signatures, such as ugly_enum_func(e: ugly_enum.MyEnum = MyEnum.ValueA) → None, are rendered in a clear and user-friendly format.
feature1.hint_texts: Enhance the object_description function in sphinx/util/inspect.py by adding a new conditional branch that checks if the object is an instance of enum.Enum. When it is, return a string formatted as 'EnumClassName.MemberName'. Make sure that this change is added after the existing conditions for sets and frozensets, and that it does not break other functionality. The modification should integrate smoothly into the current if/elif structure.
feature1.entrypoint: Modify the file sphinx/util/inspect.py in the object_description function. The new code should be inserted after the conditions handling frozenset, adding an elif block to check for isinstance(object, enum.Enum) and return the formatted output.

feature2.prompt: Python Enum values (used to show default values in function signatures) are rendered ugly. The issue is that enum members are displayed using their full internal representation, which is confusing and unfriendly to the end user. This feature focuses on verifying that the new formatting correctly displays enum values in a clean and consistent manner. The expected result is that enum members appear as just the type and member name (for example, MyEnum.ValueA) instead of the verbose internal format.
feature2.hint_texts: Add a new unit test in tests/test_util_inspect.py that ensures the enum formatting is correct. The test should define a sample enum and invoke the object_description function on an enum member, asserting that the returned string matches the expected clean format. This test is intended to fail before the core functionality is updated and pass after the changes. Ensure that the new test is isolated and integrates well with the existing test suite.
feature2.entrypoint: Modify the file tests/test_util_inspect.py by adding a new test function named test_object_description_enum. This function should create a sample enum class, call object_description on one of its members, and assert that the output matches the expected format.

collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature 1 implements the enhanced enum formatting in the object_description function, while Feature 2 introduces a dedicated test to verify this new behavior. Both features affect the same core functionality and utilize the same test file, ensuring that the implementation and its validation are tightly integrated.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on Feature 1 and Feature 2 must coordinate to agree on the expected output format for enum values. They should discuss the ordering of conditional checks in the object_description function and confirm that the new test accurately reflects the intended behavior. Regular communication will help ensure that the integration of the core change with its tests is seamless and meets the overall design goals.
